route: B. Le Cam two-point impossibility for the 32-pilot and explicit failing worlds inside the compatible set (lower bound; necessity direction)
statement: Le Cam two-point bound for the ACTUAL two-type pilot, with exact constants and the exact (Neyman–Pearson) minima. For the G6 h_3 pilot (100 type-0 + 100 type-1 prefixes, m `sel` counts each, K_i|r_i ~ Bin(m, r_i), r iid ~ F_t within type), every pre-experiment decision rule (randomized allowed; any compatible-set construction) that decides whether to certify (200,128) satisfies P_{F_a}(do not certify) + P_{F_b}(certify) >= 1 - sqrt(1 - rho_0^{200} rho_1^{200}), and the minimum over all rules equals 1 - TV(P_a, P_b), attained by the likelihood-ratio test. Anchor pair F_a = Beta(20,80)/Beta(25,75) vs F_b = Beta(40.5,162)/Beta(50.6,151.8) at m=32: bound 0.41943 (the problem phase's 0.569 is the TYPE-0 FACTOR rho_0^{100} alone, reproduced exactly as 0.56936, not the pilot's bound); exact minimum 0.5210 +- 0.0014 (0.5233 +- 0.0014 with a second seed). Exact two-point world F_c2 (rational atoms 81/505, 6/25 w 101/201, 100/201; 329/1616, 29/100 w 1616/3491, 1875/3491; same mean AND variance as F_a per type): bound 0.81069, exact minimum 0.8537 +- 0.0016. At the 128-stage (m=128 counts): exact minima 0.0967 (F_b), 0.1638 (F_c2), 0.5499 (F_theta=0.8), 0.7721 (F_theta=0.9); at m=512: 0.0060 (F_b), 0.3561 (F_0.8), 0.6581 (F_0.9). Corollary: any rule with false-certification probability P_b(certify) <= gamma has P_a(certify) <= TV + gamma, so a certificate valid at gamma=0.05 against F_c2 is available in the narrow world at most 19.6% of the time, against F_b at most 52.9%.
scope: Holds for any stated compatible-set construction (DKW, multinomial likelihood, moment-based) and any pre-experiment rule, in the iid-within-type binomial-count model, for the listed pairs at m in {32,128,512}; the Hellinger bound is one-sided (a small bound does not prove separability) and the NP column is the exact value for these specific pairs only.
does_not_claim: It does not claim the bound is attained by any rule restricted to a practical class (only the LR test attains it); it does not cover rules that use the steered-arm outcomes; it does not cover within-question dependence of r (the constants would change; with positive dependence the effective pilot is smaller); it does not claim that worlds other than the listed ones are farther from F_a (the sup over the compatible set may be obstructed by closer worlds).
assumptions: Pilot counts independent across prefixes given risks and K_i|r_i ~ Bin(m, r_i) exactly (design: selection on y_2 text and e_2=0 only, never on counts; sec 7.2b D4).
Within type t the risks are iid ~ F_t (template model class); question clustering enters only through r and is not modelled in the bound.
The rule is a measurable (possibly randomized) function of the 200 pilot counts only: pre-experiment relative to Delta_hat; reuse of the 32 inside the 128 adds no information at the pilot stage.

n_0 = n_1 = 100 (equal type counts); Beta parameters rational so that the count pmfs are exactly rational (Beta(40.5,162) = (81/2,162), Beta(50.6,151.8) = (253/5,759/5)); affinities evaluated at 60 significant digits (mpmath) from the exact fractions, the square root being the only irrational step.

The NP-exact minima are Monte Carlo estimates of the LR test's error sum (200,000 pilots per side; ties counted as 'not certify', so they are upper bounds on the minimum that coincide with it up to tie mass).
experimental_consequence: Outcome (a) '32 already certified' of the sequential rule is unattainable in the narrow regime for ANY certificate construction: a certificate with ≤5% false certification against the exact two-point world fires under F_a at most 20% of the time (53% against F_b). The plan's decision must therefore be written as 'adopt 128 as a PRE-SPECIFIED pilot extension and re-assess at 128'. At the 128-stage, under the proposed tolerances (q90 width ≤ 0.15, non-PD ≤ 2%), outcome (c) '128 certified at the 128-stage' is itself obstructed by F_theta=0.9 / 0.8 (exact minimal error sums 0.77 / 0.55 at m=128), whereas under relaxed tolerances (q90 ≤ 0.20, non-PD ≤ 3%) the obstruction pair becomes F_0.7 with 0.355: the residual risk carried to the 128-stage is a tolerance decision for the user, not a fact about the data. The archive constant '0.569' must be corrected to 'type-0 factor; actual pilot 0.419 (bound) / 0.52 (exact)'.

route: B. Le Cam two-point impossibility for the 32-pilot and explicit failing worlds inside the compatible set (lower bound; necessity direction)
statement: The failure of F_b at (200,128) is a property of the count design and persists over the bounded g-class and both SEs; F_a passes (marginally) and every examined non-degenerate world passes at 512. Under the null b_type = 0 with y_i = c + b_1 r_i + b_2 r_i^2 + eta_i, the production score is psi_{i,a} = b_1 (U_a r_i - U_{a+1}) + b_2 (U_a r_i^2 - U_{a+2}) + U_a eta_i (c cancels exactly) and the corrected matrix A = sum_i M_i depends on (K, t) only, so the PD event {ok = True} of endpoint_contrast_poly_cs is identical for every g, every Var(eta|r) and HC1 vs CR1 (verified bit-for-bit on 300 draws x 10 g x 3 eta-laws x 2 SEs = 18,000 production calls). Consequently the non-PD rate alone decides F_b's failure for the whole class: pooled over the 10-point g-grid at m=128 it is 0.1235, exact 95% CI [0.1190, 0.1281] (20,000 reps) > 2%; on the grid the PD-conditional 90th-percentile CI width is 0.43–0.64 (q90 = inf under the non-PD convention) and the size 0.0185–0.0305 (conservative side), HC1 and CR1 alike. F_a at 128: non-PD 0.0056 [0.0046, 0.0067], size 0.042–0.0535 (HC1) / 0.0465–0.060 (CR1), q90 width with inf-convention 0.136–0.1496 (HC1, all 10 g pass) and 0.139–0.1531 (CR1: 9 of 10 pass; g_4 = -0.2 + 1.2r fails the 0.15 width by 0.003). At m=512: F_a, F_b, F_c2 and F_theta (0.6–0.9) pass for every grid g and both SEs (non-PD 0 [0, 0.00018]; q90 ≤ 0.141; size 0.0455–0.067). The exact two-point F_c2 has D = 0.1829 = D(F_a) yet fails at 128 (non-PD 0.1153 [0.1074, 0.1237]; q90|ok 0.277–0.284) — the failure is the PD margin of E[S_w(128)] against the U-statistic noise (lambda_min 2.9e-6 for F_c2 and 2.8e-6 for F_b vs 8.0e-6 for F_a), not the type coefficient's population identification strength D. Variance-scale worlds fail at 128 only marginally: F_0.9 q90 0.158/0.163, non-PD 1.2%; F_0.8 q90 0.188/0.192, non-PD 2.3% [1.7, 3.1]%; F_0.7 q90 0.315, non-PD 4.15%; F_0.6 q90 1.75, non-PD 7.5%.
scope: Finite-sample statements at (n, m) = (200, 128) and (200, 512) under the stated DGP; the non-PD invariance (and hence F_b's failure of the non-PD ≤ 2% tolerance) holds for the entire bounded g-class, every Var(eta|r) and both SEs; the width/size statements hold on the 10-point g-grid with the quoted MC uncertainty.
does_not_claim: It does not claim that width or size are bounded over the whole g-class (the Chebyshev-extreme g = 8r^2-8r+1 satisfies |g| ≤ 1 but violates q_± in [0,1] in the narrow world and was not run); it does not claim F_a passes for every g under CR1 (g_4 fails the 0.15 width by 0.003) or that the pass at 128 is robust to the tolerance (q90 0.136–0.153 straddles 0.15); it says nothing about power, about the two-stage reuse size (route C), or about worlds outside the examined families.
assumptions: Production function endpoint_contrast_poly_cs(degree=2, PD rule lambda_min > 1e-9·max(1, lambda_max), HC1 default, CR1 with cluster) imported from g6_iv.py; no re-implementation.
n = 200 = 100 per type; counts K ~ Bin(m, r) with m in {128, 512} common to all prefixes; null b_type = 0.
eta = difference of two independent 16-draw binomial means with q_± = clip(r ± g/2, 0, 1); clip rates recorded per cell (≤ 6.1e-4 on the grid).
CR1 clusters: 50 questions, each with 2 type-0 and 2 type-1 prefixes (K_pref = 4); r iid (no question effect), so CR1 is a robustness choice.
2000 replications per cell (size MC SE ≈ 0.005, non-PD SE ≈ 0.007); one seed per cell (base 4242 + 1000·index); exact Clopper–Pearson intervals reported.
experimental_consequence: The 'adopt 128 → (d) 128 insufficient → 512' branch is a genuine event whose probability no 32-pilot rule can drive down (B1), but 512 (4×, still vLLM) passed in every examined non-degenerate world (F_b, F_c2, F_theta 0.6–0.9, all grid g, both SEs), so 512 is a defensible pre-registered fallback; F_lp and the point mass (branch (e), unidentified) fail at 512 too and are the only examined worlds where 512 does not help. The size failure at F_b is on the conservative side (0.02–0.03), so the pre-registered test does not over-reject there; the binding failures are non-PD and width. The q90 ≤ 0.15 tolerance puts the narrow world itself on a knife edge (0.136–0.153 across g and SE), so the plan should pre-register the tolerance with a stated sensitivity (0.15 vs 0.20) and should state that CR1 with 50 clusters of 2+2 widens q90 by ≈ 0.003–0.005 relative to HC1.

route: B. Le Cam two-point impossibility for the 32-pilot and explicit failing worlds inside the compatible set (lower bound; necessity direction)
statement: The stated compatible set of a narrow pilot contains the failing and nearly-unidentified worlds, and a non-Beta compatible world with a negative A1 Schur margin exists. With C_gamma^DKW = {F : sup_k |G_{F,t}(k) - Ghat_t(k)| ≤ eps_100(gamma) for both types}, eps_n(gamma) = sqrt(ln(2/gamma)/(2n)) (0.1358 / 0.1224 / 0.0991 at gamma = 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.28; DKW–Massart holds for discrete count laws, observed coverage of F_a 0.9856 per type, 0.970 jointly at gamma = 0.05), the inclusion probabilities over 5000 narrow pilots are: F_b 0.962 / 0.916 / 0.736; F_c2 0.971 / 0.941 / 0.778; F_theta=0.8 0.968 / 0.932 / 0.769; point mass F_c (D = 0) 0.921 / 0.852 / 0.616; F_d (double variance) 0.959 / 0.905 / 0.692. Hence with probability ≥ 0.92 (gamma = 0.05) the sup over C_gamma of the non-PD rate at 128 is ≥ 0.89 and of the width is infinite (point mass), and even under a D ≥ d_0 restriction the sup is ≥ 0.1235 / q90 ≥ 0.43 with probability 0.97 (F_c2 has D = D(F_a)). An LP over grid mixtures x_j = j/400 inside the gamma = 0.05 band with the true (mu_1, mu_2) fixed, minimizing v^T E[S_t(128)] v in the lambda_min-direction of F_a (objective affine in (mu_3, mu_4) through A1's exact joint moments, hence linear in w), yields F_lp with 3 atoms per type (type 0: {0.18, 0.1825, 0.285} w {0.368, 0.452, 0.180}; type 1: {0.1875, 0.2775, 0.28} w {0.322, 0.083, 0.595}), pooled lambda_min E[S_w(128)] = -1.29e-7 (vs +7.99e-6 at F_a), D = 0.0244, lambda_min(H̄_w) = 7.4e-9, production non-PD 0.6445 [0.623, 0.666] at 128 and 0.583 [0.561, 0.605] at 512 (width q50|ok 0.20 / 0.29, oracle q50 0.255); F_lp is inseparable from F_a at m=32 (NP-exact minimal error sum 0.670 ± 0.0015; Hellinger 0.592) but separable at m=128 (0.032 ± 0.0004). The LP range of V inside the band with mu_1 fixed is [0, 0.039] (true V_a = 0.00158).
scope: Existence statements for explicit worlds under one stated confidence construction (DKW, any gamma) in the narrow regime; inclusion frequencies are MC estimates with SE ≤ 0.007; the LP value is a valid upper bound on min_{F in C_gamma} lambda_min E[S_w(128)] (equivalently a lower bound on how bad the compatible set is).
does_not_claim: It does not claim the LP solution is the extreme point of C_gamma (a fixed direction replaced the concave minimization, and extreme points were not shown extremal); it does not claim a multinomial-likelihood region contains the same worlds with the same probabilities (its constants differ; B1 bounds every construction); it does not claim F_lp is a plausible generative model for h_3 risks — it is an information-theoretic witness; it does not claim the DKW set's width in V ([0, 0.039]) is representative of moment-based constructions (the U-statistic V_hat has sd 0.00095, check2).
assumptions: Pilot = 100 type-t counts at m = 32 from F_a = Beta(20,80)/Beta(25,75); DKW band per type with the Massart constant (valid for any distribution function, discrete included, via the quantile transform).
Inclusion of a world means both types' count CDFs lie inside their bands; MC over 5000 pilots (SE ≤ 0.007), seed 777.

LP: grid atoms j/400 (j = 1..399), simplex weights, DKW inequalities at k = 0..31, equalities mu_1, mu_2 fixed at the true values (variant with the pilot's U-statistic estimates also run: pooled minimum -1.68e-7); objective direction v = eigenvector of lambda_min of the pooled E[S_w(128)] at F_a; HiGHS solver; E[U_a U_b] coefficients from the production binomial_factorial_joint_moment on unit moment vectors.
Production test at F_lp: endpoint_contrast_poly_cs degree 2, HC1 and CR1, g_1 = 0.18 - 0.8r, 16-draw arms, 2000 reps, seeds 100119 (m=128) and 100503 (m=512).
F_lp's pmfs and affinities in float64 (its atoms are grid rationals but weights are LP floats); the named worlds' constants are exact (B1).
experimental_consequence: A route-A certificate built on the DKW compatible set cannot fire in the narrow world at any gamma ≤ 0.28 unless it excludes D < d_0 worlds by assumption, and even then F_c2 (same D as F_a) remains inside with probability 0.97 and fails at 128 — so the certificate's 'excluded worlds' must be stated in terms of the PD margin of E[S_w(128)] against the U-statistic noise (a kurtosis-type constraint on F), i.e. as a model-class assumption the user accepts, not as something the pilot verifies. The 'unidentified' branch (e) cannot be excluded at the 32-stage (point mass and F_lp inside the set with probability 0.92 / inseparable at 0.67) but its examined witnesses are separable at the 128-stage (NP minima 0.17e-? — exact: F_lp 0.032, point mass bound 4e-8), so the 128-stage re-assessment can detect non-identification even though it cannot certify sufficiency under the proposed tolerances.

route: A. Overlap-and-PD-margin certificate from pilot U-statistics (upper bound; sufficiency direction)
statement: First-order (asymptotic) sandwich of the degree-2 corrected-score TYPE coefficient in closed form: with x=(1,r,r^2), Q_xx=Σ_t w_t E_t[xx'], q=w_1(1,μ_{1,1},μ_{2,1})', γ=Q_xx^{-1}q and the overlap D(F)=w_1−q'Q_xx^{-1}q=min_c E[(t−c'x)^2] (per-type moments ≤4), one has Q^{-1}e_type=D^{-1}(−γ,1)' and Var_1(b̂_type)=n^{-1}D^{-2}Σ_t w_t E_t[φ^2], φ=ψ_type−γ'ψ_x, where E[φ^2|r,t]=σ^2(r)[ρ^2+γ̃'V^{(2)}(r)γ̃]+Σ_{b,d∈{1,2}}β_bβ_d α_b(r,t)'V^{(4)}(r)α_d(r,t), ρ=t−γ'x, V^{(k)}(r)_{jl}=Cov(U_j,U_l|r)=J_{jl}(r)−r^{j+l} with J_{jl}(r)=Σ_ℓ C(j,ℓ)C(l,ℓ)ℓ!(m)_{j+l−ℓ}/((m)_j(m)_l) r^{j+l−ℓ} (A1 identity per r), and α_{b,j}=−(t−γ_0)1[j=b]−γ_1 r^b 1[j=1]+γ_1 1[j=1+b]−γ_2 r^b 1[j=2]+γ_2 1[j=2+b]. Hence the first-order 95% width w_1=3.92·sqrt(Σ_t w_t E_t φ^2/(nD^2)) is an explicit polynomial functional of per-type moments ≤8 (the A1 bound min(m,4p)=8 is attained), w_1, m, n, g and σ^2(·); as m→∞ it reduces to the oracle OLS width 3.92·sqrt(E[ρ^2σ^2]/(nD^2)). Over the response class {|g|≤1 on [0,1]} with σ^2≤r(1−r)/8 the g-term is a PSD quadratic β'Ωβ whose sup is attained on the boundary osc(β_1 r+β_2 r^2)=2 (Chebyshev extreme g=1−8r+8r^2 in all worlds computed).
scope: Holds for any F_t with finite support in [0,1] or any law identified by its moments ≤8, any m≥4, any n, both HC1 and CR1; it is the population (n→∞) sandwich, verified exactly (Fractions) against brute-force enumeration for discrete laws at m∈{4,8,10}, w_1∈{1/2,2/5}, and against the production function at n=20000 (ratio of production √n·se to the formula 1.000–1.007 ± 0.01 at m=128 in narrow/half-variance/wide and at m=32 wide).
does_not_claim: It does not claim the finite-sample width distribution at n=200 is governed by w_1: at m=32 in the narrow/half-variance worlds the production se is heavy-tailed even at n=20000 (half-variance m=32: ratio 1.20 ± 0.37) and at n=200 the realised q90 exceeds w_1 (archive check1/check1b medians 0.114/0.176 vs w_1 0.107/0.143 at m=128); it does not bound the non-PD rate or the size.
assumptions: r_i|t_i iid ~F_t within type, prefixes independent, n_t fixed (100 each), no question effect in r or Δ beyond r
K_i|r_i ~ Bin(m,r_i), common m; U_j(K)=(K)_j/(m)_j
y_i=β_0+β_1 r_i+β_2 r_i^2+b_type t_i+η_i with E[η|r,t,K]=0, Var(η|r)=σ^2(r) (two independent 16-draw arms, q_±=r±g/2 unclipped gives σ^2=[2r(1−r)−g^2/2]/16 ≤ r(1−r)/8; with clipping only σ^2≤1/32)
Q_xx invertible and D>0 (fails in the point-mass 0.20/0.25 world: D=0, w_1=∞)
first order = LLN/CLT limit of Â^{-1}Σψ_i; HC1 and CR1 estimate the same B at first order
experimental_consequence: Gives the plan §7.11 a closed-form width criterion at any m (the 'first-order width and population PD margin' closed forms the obstacle asked for); it shows the width tolerance q90≤0.15 cannot be met uniformly over the full class |g|≤1 at (200,128) in the narrow world (sup 0.164) but can for coefficient-bounded g (0.119) — so the response class is a user decision that changes the 128 verdict; it does NOT by itself license m=32 (first-order width 0.144 there while the actual test is 54% non-PD).

route: A. Overlap-and-PD-margin certificate from pilot U-statistics (upper bound; sufficiency direction)
statement: Pilot certificate C(pilot; m, G', d_0, w_0): from the 32 (or 128) α=0 counts, per-type moment vector θ̂_t=mean_i U_{1..8}(K_i) (unbiased), question-cluster covariance, delta-method one-sided 95% bounds; fires iff LCB(D)≥d_0 and UCB(sup_{g∈G'} w_1(m))≤w_0 (optional third condition on the A1 PD margin κ(m)=λ_min(E[S_w(m)], N̄(m)), moments ≤4). By derivation: when it fires, D≥d_0 and the first-order width ≤w_0 for every (F,g) in the asymptotic confidence set × G'; the plug-in D̂ is biased downward (D concave in the moments, θ̂ unbiased ⇒ E[D̂]≤D, conservative in the mean). Availability and conditional (two-stage, internal-pilot) size/width validity are to be read from the production-function simulation a2_two_stage_sim.py (4000 reps per linear-g world, 2000 per quadratic-g cell), which was still running at reporting time; single-pilot evaluations show the expected pattern (wide pilot: D̂=0.229 LCB 0.213, UCB(w_1 at 128, full class) 0.122 ⇒ fires; narrow pilot: D̂=0.145 with delta-sd 0.12, half-variance pilot: D̂=0.089 sd 0.20 ⇒ cannot fire).
scope: The certificate's first-order guarantee holds for every F in the stated delta-method confidence set with D≥d_0 and every g∈G'; its availability and its finite-sample validity (size, non-PD, q90 width at the target under reuse) are world-specific simulation quantities for the three Beta worlds and the two g's of the design.
does_not_claim: It does not claim finite-sample size or non-PD control by derivation (no explicit-constant bound exists at n=200 by the tools of A-C3; CE-B1 shows low moments do not determine them); it does not claim the sup over the confidence set is attained at extreme points; it does not claim availability numbers until a2_summary.json exists — the narrow-world unavailability is predicted (pilot noise exceeds the r^2-after-r signal, λ_min(H_w)≈8e-6, check2) but not yet measured by this route.
assumptions: same model as A-C1
delta-method confidence set (asymptotic, n_t=100); one-sided γ=0.05 per component, Bonferroni over the two components
σ^2≤r(1−r)/8 (no clipping) used inside the certificate; clipping rate reported by the simulation
the simulated design: 50 questions × (2 type-0 + 2 type-1), r iid (no question effect), K128=K32+K96 reuse, η from 16+16 draws, null b_type=0
experimental_consequence: Defines the pre-specifiable 32-stage and 128-stage rules for plan §7.2b/§7.11 (fire ⇒ certify m; otherwise extend); the decision numbers (availability per world, false-fire rate in the half-variance world, reuse-vs-fresh size difference) are pending a2_summary.json and must be filled before the gate decision is written.

route: A. Overlap-and-PD-margin certificate from pilot U-statistics (upper bound; sufficiency direction)
statement: The explicit-constant finite-sample branch of the certificate is vacuous at the G6 pilot size (100 prefixes per type, m=32) in all three worlds: (i) the Hoeffding/Bonferroni moment box (ε_H=sqrt(ln(640)/200)=0.1797 over 16 moments; 0.1593 over 4) contains the two-point-mass moment vector θ* (μ_{j,t}=μ̂_{1,t}^j) whenever max_{t,j}|μ̂_{j,t}−μ̂_{1,t}^j|≤ε_H, and θ* has D=0 and w_1=∞; this held in 5000/5000 pilots per world (max deviation 0.0069 narrow, 0.0050 half-var, 0.0301 wide), so inf_{box} D=0 and no d_0>0 or finite w_0 can ever be certified; (ii) the per-type DKW band (ε_D=0.148) contains a two-point-per-type world with supports {a,b},{c,d}, a+b=c+d (D=0 exactly) in 20/20 pilots per world (sup-distances 0.025–0.050 narrow, 0.011–0.061 half-var, 0.036–0.080 wide); (iii) matrix Bernstein for ||Ā−Q||<λ_min(Q) with exact σ_1^2 and R from the Beta-binomial law needs n≈1.1e11 (narrow), 8.6e11 (half-var), 6.0e7 (wide), and the whitened version n≈1.2e5–1.4e5 (narrow), 3.5e5–4.1e5 (half-var), 2.5e3–2.8e3 (wide), versus n=200.
scope: Holds for these three exact constructions at (n_t,m)=(100,32) (Bernstein also at m=128) in the narrow, half-variance and wide Beta worlds; the Hoeffding statement is a proof for every pilot whose max deviation is ≤ε_H (all 15000 simulated); the DKW statement is a proof for each pilot in which a D=0 world was found (60/60).
does_not_claim: It does not claim that no exact finite-sample certificate exists (only that boxes on moments, DKW bands on counts and matrix-Bernstein on the corrected matrix cannot give one at this size), nor that the asymptotic delta-method set of A-C2 has exact coverage.
assumptions: U_j(K)∈[0,1]; per-type counts iid (Hoeffding applies); Bonferroni over 2 types × 8 orders at γ=0.05
DKW at γ'=0.025 per type on the count CDF; the D=0 family is binomial mixtures with two support points per type and a+b=c+d (then t=κ(r−a)(r−b) exactly)
matrix Bernstein (Tropp) with d=4, s=λ_min(Q), σ_1^2=||E(M̂−Q)^2||, R=max_K||M̂−Q||, computed from the exact Beta-binomial count law of each world
experimental_consequence: Removes 'rigorous finite-sample certificate with explicit constants at n=200' from the plan's options: any pre-specified pilot rule for §7.11 must be an asymptotic (delta-method / bootstrap) construction whose coverage is simulation-checked, and the non-PD ≤2% tolerance cannot be guaranteed by concentration inequalities — it stays a simulation-calibrated quantity.

route: C. Sequential internal-pilot design: 32 → 128 → re-assess, and validity under reuse
statement: Uniform reuse bound (Theorem 1). Let R be any event of the final degree-2 corrected-score test at m=128 (reject = ok & |t|>1.96 with ok=False counted as non-rejection; non-PD; width ≤ w0) computed on K = K32 + K96 (reuse), and R' the same functional on fresh K'128 ⊥ K32 given r. For EVERY stage-1 rule D measurable w.r.t. (t, K32) with P(D) = π: P(R|D) − P(R'|D) = Cov(δ, 1_D)/π with δ := P(R|t,K32) − P(R'|t,K32), E[δ] = 0, hence |P(R|D) − P(R'|D)| ≤ σ_δ·sqrt((1−π)/π), σ_δ² = Var(δ); the selection term P(R'|D) − P(R) obeys the same bound with σ_0² = Var(P(R'|t,K32)). The identity needs only A0 (η independent of all counts given r); the sup over rules is attained by the upper-tail rule {δ > q_{1−π}}. Mechanism (Proposition 2): the only pilot-tiltable part of the corrected score is φ_i = E[ψ_i | r_i, K32_i] = g(r_i)Ũ_a − Σ_b β_b Ũ_{a+b}, Ũ_j(k,r) = C(128,j)^{-1} Σ_l C(k,l)C(96,j−l) r^{j−l}; Φ = Var(φ_i) ⪯ Σ^{ME} = Var(d_i) ⪯ Σ, Ũ_1 − r = (32/128)(r̂32 − r) exactly (pilot share of the ME variance of U_1 is exactly 1/4; of U_2 it is 0.2477 narrow / 0.2476 half-variance / 0.2485 wide, exact rationals in c3_tilt_moments.json); along the population type direction the maximal standardized first-order mean tilt at P(D)=1/2 is κ = 0.093/0.083/0.230 (narrow, g = lin/quad/cheb), 0.087/0.077/0.209 (half-variance), 0.099/0.088/0.243 (wide). Nested Monte Carlo with the production function (1000 outer pilots × 200 inner, common random numbers, one-way ANOVA estimator proved unbiased) gives for the REJECT event the 95% upper limits σ_δ ≤ 0.0064 (narrow lin HC1) / 0.0051 (CR1), 0.0041/0.0038 (narrow quad), 0.0085/0.0075 (narrow cheb), 0.0047/0.0061 (half-variance lin), i.e. the reuse effect on the two-stage size of ANY 32-pilot rule with P(D) ≥ 0.5 is ≤ 0.0085 and with P(D) ≥ 0.1 is ≤ 0.026 (cheb) / ≤ 0.019 (archive g); for the NON-PD and WIDTH ≤ 0.15 events σ_δ is NOT small in the half-variance world (0.036 and 0.085), because the production ok flag is a deterministic function of the counts and the pilot's PD status propagates into K32+K96.
scope: Holds for every pilot rule that is a function of the 32 α=0 sel counts and types, for every event of the final 128-test, under A0; the quoted constants σ_δ apply to the four named (world, g) cells with the stated 16-draw arms and the degree-2 production test at (200,128), HC1 and CR1 (50 clusters of 4, both types in each cluster).
does_not_claim: It does not bound |P(R|D) − 0.05|: the one-stage size at 128 itself (0.045 narrow, 0.022 half-variance) and the selection-on-configuration term (σ_0 ≤ 0.0063) are separate; it does not give a closed form for σ_δ, does not cover rules that see the steered-arm outcomes, does not cover the sup over the compatible set of risk laws or over the full class |g| ≤ 1 (only three members), and does not establish that the width or non-PD two-stage rates are within tolerance (their σ_δ are 0.03–0.085 in the half-variance world).
assumptions: A0: η_i (difference of two independent 16-draw binomial means) is independent of (K32, K96, K'128) given r and independent across prefixes; prefixes independent given risks; K32 ~ Bin(32,r), K96 ~ Bin(96,r), K'128 ~ Bin(128,r) independent given r (so K32+K96 ~ Bin(128,r)).
Pilot rules are σ(t, K32)-measurable with P(D) ∈ (0,1); the final test is the production endpoint_contrast_poly_cs(degree=2) on the same 200 prefixes (n_t = 100), null b_type = 0.

For the Monte Carlo constants: risks Beta per type (narrow (20,80)/(25,75); half-variance (40.5,162)/(50.6,151.8)), g ∈ {0.18−0.8r, 0.26−1.6r+2r², 0.5(1−8r+8r²)} with q_± = clip(r ± g/2) (clip rate ≤ 1.9e-4), r | K32 drawn from the exact Beta posterior; question clusters 50 × 4 (2 per type) with no effect beyond r (HC1 valid, CR1 reported as robustness).

Theorem 1 and Proposition 2 hold for any risk law; the exact moment evaluation in c3 uses Beta moments and the A1 identity; the σ_δ constants are estimated (outer-bootstrap 95% upper limits), not derived.
experimental_consequence: The internal-pilot design (keep the 32 sel counts inside the 128) is admissible for the SIZE target without fresh regressor continuations: for every stage-1 adoption rule with P(adopt) ≥ 0.1 the reuse effect on the two-stage size is below the ±0.02 tolerance in the archive g worlds (≤ 0.019 narrow, ≤ 0.014 half-variance) and marginally above it only for the extreme member g = 0.5(1−8r+8r²) at P(D)=0.1 (0.026); the user does not need to spend 32 extra draws per prefix on a fresh regressor. The non-PD ≤ 2% and q90-width ≤ 0.15 tolerances are NOT protected by this theorem (σ_δ up to 0.085): the plan must state them as one-stage (fresh-equivalent) targets at 128 or evaluate them conditionally on the adopted rule.

route: C. Sequential internal-pilot design: 32 → 128 → re-assess, and validity under reuse
statement: Rule-specific reuse and selection terms (stage 1, 32 → 128, production test, HC1 and CR1), estimated with common random numbers to SE ≈ 0.0006–0.0009 (10× finer than the problem-phase check3). (i) The proposed stage-1 rule 'adopt 128 = not certify-32' (certify-32 := A32 PD and width proxy w_pred(K32; σ̄²_η = 1/32) ≤ 0.15; it fires with P = 0.896–0.910 narrow, 0.987 half-variance) has |size_reuse − size_fresh| ≤ 0.0009 ± 0.0006 in all four cells (narrow lin −0.0005 ± 0.0006, quad −0.0002 ± 0.0006, cheb +0.0004 ± 0.0006, half-variance +0.0007 ± 0.0004; CR1 within ±0.001 ± 0.0006) and a selection term |P(R'|D) − P(R)| ≤ 0.0003. (ii) Rules keyed to pilot spread or PD status ('V̂32 > median', 'PD at 32', 'PD-margin-128 estimate > median') show a SIGNIFICANT positive reuse effect in the half-variance world: +0.0030 ± 0.0006, +0.0027 ± 0.0008, +0.0022 ± 0.0006 (HC1; CR1 +0.0033, +0.0028, +0.0025), which is entirely the non-PD channel (non-PD given fire 9.7% / 8.9% / 9.8% with reuse vs 11.7% / 12.0% / 12.0% fresh; non-PD counts as non-rejection) — the pilot's PD status carries into K32+K96; in the narrow world (non-PD 0.5%) the same rules give ≤ +0.003 ± 0.0009 (lin: −0.0007, +0.0004, +0.0002; cheb: +0.0012, +0.0029, +0.0025). (iii) The plug-in adversarial rule (upper half of the estimated δ_o) gives +0.013 to +0.017 — an upward-biased plug-in sup consistent with Theorem 1's bound 0.005–0.009 at P(D) = 1/2 only as an over-estimate, and the direction of every detected effect is positive (reuse raises the rejection rate through fewer non-PD outcomes).
scope: Four (world, g) cells at (n, m) = (200, 32→128), 1000 outer × 200 inner, HC1 and CR1 (50 clusters of 4); rule classes listed; sizes are unconditional (ok & |t| > 1.96).
does_not_claim: It does not establish the conditional operating characteristics of the degree-2 test AT m = 32 when certify-32 fires (the 32-test was not run in the inner loop), does not cover the wide world (cell still running), does not prove the sign of the reuse effect in general, and the plug-in adversarial value is not a valid bound (winner's curse).
assumptions: Same DGP and A0 as C1; rules evaluated on the outer pilot draws; the 'certify-32' width proxy omits the measurement-error term d_i d_iᵀ of the sandwich and uses σ̄²_η = sup_r Var(η|r) = 1/32 (plug-in 0.02 variant also reported).
Thresholds 'median' are in-sample medians over the 1000 outer pilots (as in check3).
experimental_consequence: The specific adoption rule proposed for the plan (adopt 128 unless the 32-stage certificate fires) can be pre-registered with the 32 counts reused: its reuse term is ≤ 0.001 in every cell. Rules keyed to the pilot's PD status or spread are also admissible for size (effects +0.002–0.003, inside ±0.02) but they bias the final non-PD rate downward by 2–3 points in weak worlds, so the non-PD ≤ 2% tolerance must be assessed conditionally on the rule, not from one-stage tables.

route: C. Sequential internal-pilot design: 32 → 128 → re-assess, and validity under reuse
statement: Stage-2 re-assessment is well-defined without steered arms and the decision tree can be pre-specified: (F1) the production ok flag at 128 is a deterministic function of (K128, t) — the non-PD outcome of the final degree-2 test is KNOWN at the 128 stage; (F2) the HC1 sandwich decomposes as E[Σψψᵀ | r,K] = Σ_i Var(η_i|r_i) û_i û_iᵀ + Σ_i d_i d_iᵀ, so the outcome-noise part of the width is a known function of the counts given a bound σ̄²_η ≤ 1/32, giving the pre-specified rule R128: not PD ⇒ 512; PD and w_pred(K128; σ̄²_η) ≤ 0.15 ⇒ certify 128; else 512. Stage-1 operating characteristics (four cells): the stage-1 certificate R32 fires in 9–10% of narrow pilots and 1.3% of half-variance pilots (with the plug-in σ̄²_η = 0.02: 19% / 4.8%), so 'adopt 128' is the overwhelmingly likely branch in both non-wide worlds; the unconditional 128-test has (size, non-PD, width q50/q90): narrow lin HC1 (0.045, 0.6%, 0.113/0.143) — within all three tolerances; narrow cheb (0.042, 0.6%, 0.127/0.171) — size within, q90 width FAILS 0.15 inside the admissible class |g| ≤ 1/2; half-variance (0.022, 11.9%, 0.187/∞) — fails size, non-PD and width, so the 128-stage must escalate. The 128-stage availability of R128 and the 512-branch reuse constant were NOT obtained (stage-2 simulation still running at the deadline).
scope: Decision-tree structure (F1, F2, R32/R128 definitions) holds generally; the operating characteristics are from the four stage-1 cells at (200, 32→128) with 16-draw arms, HC1/CR1.
does_not_claim: It does not give P(certify 128 | world), the conditional size/width at 128 given certification, or the 512-stage reuse bound (not computed); it does not certify 32 in the wide world from this route's own runs (wide cell pending; the archive/check1 one-stage numbers 0.050 / q90 0.096 at m = 32 are context); it does not claim the width proxy is a certificate over |g| ≤ 1.
assumptions: Same model and A0; F1 follows from the code path of endpoint_contrast_poly_cs (A = Σ M_i(K) depends on counts and types only); F2 from ψ_i = û_i η_i + d_i with E[η|r,K] = 0.
w_pred omits the d_i d_iᵀ term; its validity as a width predictor is world-dependent (at m = 32 in narrow worlds the ME term dominates, so R32 is not validated there).
experimental_consequence: Plan §7.2b/§7.11 can be changed to the sequential rule: run 128 sel continuations for the 200 h_3 prefixes unless R32 fires (it fires ≈ 10% narrow, ≈ 1% half-variance), then apply R128 at the 128 stage before any steered arm; the residual probability that 512 is needed is NOT yet quantified (stage 2 pending). The width tolerance q90 ≤ 0.15 is sensitive to g within the admissible class (0.143 for the archive g vs 0.171 for 0.5(1−8r+8r²)) and to the 16- vs 32-draw arms — a user decision.
